title: What a record!
objectives: describe extreme numerical achievements and world records

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Greet student and introduce lesson objectives for What a record!.
Welcome to today's lesson: What a record!! Today we will practice how to describe extreme numerical achievements and world records.

elements.content: Lesson Objectives for What a record!:
describe extreme numerical achievements and world records; use can for exceptional ability

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Introduce target vocabulary and key language structures using concept check questions.

elements.content: Review key terms and target language below:
Key terms: record, top, best, fast, high, number

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Check understanding through controlled choice exercise.

elements.content: What year was the world record set in the reading text?

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Develop reading comprehension and listening skills.

teacherNotes.title: Listening Tapescript
teacherNotes.content: This athlete set the best record. He can swim faster than anyone else!

elements.content: Read the short passage below (recycling introduced vocabulary):
What a record! He can run very fast and set the top world record number in 2020.
Listening Task: Listen to your teacher / audio prompt and answer the comprehension question.

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Provide communicative speaking practice and personalized interaction.

elements.content: Present an interesting world record and state what the record-breaker can do.

teacherNotes.title: Stage aim
teacherNotes.content: Review key corrections and confirm homework task.
Great work today! Remember to review target words in your mobile app before our next class.

elements.content: Today you practiced: describe extreme numerical achievements and world records, use can for exceptional ability.
